answer_1.quote: This paper focuses on the task of citing sentence generation, which entails identifying salient information from cited papers and capturing connections between cited and citing papers.

answer_2.quote: Following previous work, we report ROUGE-1 (unigram), ROUGE-2 (bigram), and ROUGE-L (longest common subsequence) scores to evaluate the generated citing sentences.

answer_4.quote: We sampled 50 instances from the generated texts. Three graduate students who are fluent in English and familiar with NLP were asked to rate citing sentences produced by BACO and the re-implemented PTGEN-Cross with respect to four aspects on a 1 (very poor) to 5 (excellent) point scale: fluency, relevance, coherence, and overall quality.
answer_4.guideline: Rate each generated citing sentence on fluency, relevance, coherence, and overall quality using a 1‑5 scale.
